title: Returned-Payment Record and Fee Relief on Ridgeline Home Improvement Financing Catch-Up Payments
content:
*Payments risk guidance, Ridgeline Home Improvement Financing.*

The borrower's returned-payment record gives the record relief share on a catch-up payment for an account whose plan carries no promotion (a fixed-rate or low-payment plan), counting payments returned unpaid in the twelve months before the payment: none returned takes the clean-record relief share of 10%; exactly one returned takes the single-return relief share of 5%; two or more give none.

Part of the fee pool, being the late fees, returned-payment fees and phone payment fees posted in the three months before the payment less the fee reversals posted in those months (a pool below zero counts as zero), is left on the balance instead of being collected in the catch-up payment. Where more than one relief share applies to the same catch-up payment, the shares are added together; the relief is the combined share times the fee pool, rounded to the cent and never more than the fee pool, and the catch-up payment is the catch-up figure less the relief, rounded to the cent and never below zero. Every amount rounded to the cent goes to the nearest cent, and an exact half cent rounds up.

The returns counted are the payments on that financing account returned unpaid by the bank and dated in the twelve months before the catch-up payment.

| Payments returned unpaid in the 12 months | Record relief share |
|---|---|
| None | 10% |
| Exactly 1 | 5% |
| 2 or more | None |

## Hypothetical illustrations

- No returns in the twelve months, fee pool 45.00, no other relief share: relief 4.50.
- One return eleven months before the payment and another fourteen months before it: only one falls in the twelve months, so 5%.
